import FormalConjecturesUtil
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«1043»

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1048

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1048](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1048)
- [EHP58] Erdős, P. and Herzog, F. and Piranian, G., *Metric properties of polynomials*.
  J. Analyse Math. (1958), 125-148.
- [Po61] Pommerenke, Ch., *On metric properties of complex polynomials*. Michigan Math. J.
  (1961), 97-115.
-/

namespace Erdos1048

open Polynomial Erdos1043

/-- The set $\{ z \in \mathbb{C} : \lvert f(z)\rvert < 1\}$ -/
def openLevelSet (f : Polynomial ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z : ℂ | ‖f.eval z‖ < 1}

/--
If $f\in \mathbb{C}[x]$ is a monic polynomial with all roots satisfying
$\lvert z\rvert \leq r$ for some $r<2$, then must
$$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert <1\}$$
have a connected component with diameter $>2-r$?

A problem of Erdős, Herzog, and Piranian [EHP58].

Pommerenke [Po61] proved the answer is no for $r>1$, showing that if $f(z)=z^n-r^n$ then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert \leq 1\}$ has $n$ connected components, all with diameter
$\to 0$ as $n\to \infty$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1048.lean"]
theorem erdos_1048 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (r : ℝ) (f : ℂ[X]), r < 2 → f.Monic → f.degree ≥ 1 → (∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) →
      ∃ z ∈ openLevelSet f, ENNReal.ofReal (2 - r) <
        Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (openLevelSet f) z) := by
  sorry

/--
Pommerenke [Po61] proved the answer is no for $r>1$, showing that if $f(z)=z^n-r^n$ then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert \leq 1\}$ has $n$ connected components, all with diameter
$\to 0$ as $n\to \infty$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_1048.variants.pommerenke_ncard_components (r : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (f : ℂ[X]) (hf : f = (X : ℂ[X]) ^ n - C ((r : ℂ) ^ n)) :
    {C : Set ℂ | ∃ z ∈ levelSet f, C = connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) z}.ncard = n := by
  sorry

/--
Pommerenke [Po61] proved the answer is no for $r>1$, showing that if $f(z)=z^n-r^n$ then
$\{ z: \lvert f(z)\rvert \leq 1\}$ has $n$ connected components, all with diameter
$\to 0$ as $n\to \infty$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_1048.variants.pommerenke_diam_tendsto_zero (r : ℝ) (hr : 1 < r) (ε : ℝ)
    (hε : 0 < ε) :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in Filter.atTop, ∀ f : ℂ[X], f = (X : ℂ[X]) ^ n - C ((r : ℂ) ^ n) →
      ∀ z ∈ levelSet f,
        Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) z) < ENNReal.ofReal ε := by
  sorry

/--
On the other hand, if $0<r\leq 1$, then the answer is yes, as also shown by Pommerenke [Po61].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_1048.variants.r_le_one (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : 0 < r) (hr₁ : r ≤ 1) (f : ℂ[X])
    (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1) (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    ∃ z ∈ openLevelSet f, ENNReal.ofReal (2 - r) <
      Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (openLevelSet f) z) := by
  sorry

/--
If $0\leq r\leq 1/2$ then the component which contains $0$ must have diameter $\geq 2$, which
$f(z)=z^n$ shows is best possible.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_ge_two (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : 0 ≤ r) (hr₁ : r ≤ 1 / 2) (f : ℂ[X])
    (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1) (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    2 ≤ Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) 0) := by
  sorry

/--
If $0\leq r\leq 1/2$ then the component which contains $0$ must have diameter $\geq 2$, which
$f(z)=z^n$ shows is best possible.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_ge_two_is_best (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) :
    Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet ((X : ℂ[X]) ^ n)) 0) = 2 := by
  sorry

/--
If $1/2<r\leq \frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}$ then the component which contains $0$ must have
diameter $>1/r$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_gt_inv_r (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : 1 / 2 < r)
    (hr₁ : r ≤ (Real.sqrt 5 - 1) / 2) (f : ℂ[X]) (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1)
    (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (1 / r) < Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) 0) := by
  sorry

/--
If $\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}\leq r\leq 1$ then the component which contains $0$ must have
diameter $>2-r^2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem erdos_1048.variants.diam_gt_two_sub_sq (r : ℝ) (hr₀ : (Real.sqrt 5 - 1) / 2 ≤ r)
    (hr₁ : r ≤ 1) (f : ℂ[X]) (hmonic : f.Monic) (hdeg : f.degree ≥ 1)
    (hroots : ∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r) :
    ENNReal.ofReal (2 - r ^ 2) < Metric.ediam (connectedComponentIn (levelSet f) 0) := by
  sorry

end Erdos1048

findings.description: The non-strict root bound `∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ ≤ r`, together with only `r < 2`, admits `r = 0` and `f = X`. All hypotheses then hold, but the sole open sublevel component is the unit disk, whose diameter is exactly 2. The conclusion requires diameter strictly greater than 2. Consequently the recorded negative answer has an immediate zero-radius proof, using a case excluded by the original Erdős–Herzog–Piranian question. This counterexample, and the fact that X satisfies every admissible instance under the original strict root-disk hypothesis, were proved independently in `/workspace/review/scratch.lean`, without `sorryAx`.
findings.source_evidence: [EHP58], p.125, defines `D_r` by |z| < r; Problem 7 on p.142 asks: “If all the zeros of f lie in D_r (r < 2), does the set E have a component with diameter greater than 2-r?” See https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1958-05.pdf. This hypothesis forces r > 0 for a nonconstant complex polynomial. Pommerenke [Po61], p.98, instead uses the closed root disk but asks for diameter “at least 2-r,” which also avoids this zero-radius obstruction. The current https://www.erdosproblems.com/1048 wording repeats the Lean file’s combination of a closed root bound and strict diameter bound; the discrepancy is therefore inherited from that secondary formulation, rather than a transcription error relative to the website.
findings.suggested_fix: To match the original [EHP58] problem exactly, replace the main theorem’s root hypothesis by `(∀ z ∈ f.roots, ‖z‖ < r)` and update its docstring accordingly. Positivity of r then follows from the other hypotheses. If retaining the website’s closed-root formulation, explicitly impose `0 < r` to exclude the unintended degenerate counterexample.

reformulations.difference: Expresses “exactly n connected components” using the natural cardinality of a set of components represented by points, without an explicit finiteness hypothesis.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every component has a representative in the level set, and the membership requirement excludes the empty-component default. Since n ≥ 1, equality of ncard to n itself forces finiteness: an infinite set has ncard = 0. The resulting assertion is exactly finite cardinality n. The general equivalence `S.ncard = n ↔ S.Finite ∧ S.encard = n` for n > 0 was proved in scratch.

reformulations.difference: Uses an eventual uniform ε-bound over component representatives and a universally quantified polynomial constrained by equality, rather than writing a diameter limit.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For fixed r and ε > 0, `∀ᶠ n in atTop` means that some N works for every n ≥ N. The equality hypothesis eliminates f in favor of X^n − C(r^n); quantifying over all points in its level set covers precisely all components. Thus this states that every component diameter is eventually below ε, with N allowed to depend on r and ε. The eventual/ε–N equivalence and elimination of the equality-constrained polynomial were checked in Lean. The n = 0 term is harmless because the assertion is eventual.

sources_consulted: Erdős, Herzog and Piranian, Metric properties of polynomials, J. Analyse Math. 6 (1958), 125–148; especially the definitions on p.125 and Problem 7 on p.142. https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1958-05.pdf

Pommerenke, On metric properties of complex polynomials, Michigan Math. J. 8 (1961), 97–115; especially pp.97–100, Theorem 3 and its remarks. https://doi.org/10.1307/mmj/1028998561 ; PDF retrieved from https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.mmj/1028998561
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/plby/lean-proofs/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos1048.lean (the exact file cited by the formal_proof attribute)
Local repository guidance: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, AGENTS.md and PROOFS.md.
Local declarations and machinery: FormalConjectures/ErdosProblems/1043.lean; FormalConjecturesUtil/Answer.lean and Answer/Syntax.lean.

Mathlib at the supplied checkout: Polynomial degree, roots and splitting definitions; connectedComponentIn; Metric.ediam and Metric.diam; Set.ncard; ENNReal.ofReal; polynomial properness and normed-space ball diameter lemmas.
Local calibration: /workspace/past_misformalizations/INDEX.md and pr01342.md, pr01504.md, pr01442.md, pr01410.md, pr01138.md, pr04037.md, pr04057.md and pr04863.md.
review.notes: All nine declarations were checked. Pommerenke explicitly defines his lemniscate set using ≤ 1, so the closed-level lower-bound variants are faithful, including the component containing 0 at r = 1. Independent Lean checks establish origin membership, boundedness, diameter conversions, and the monomial equality examples. The linked proof contains no holes or custom axioms; after four compatibility repairs for the supplied newer Lean/Mathlib version, its proof and a bridge to the current repository statement compile with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Details are in /workspace/review/review_notes.md, scratch.lean and formal_proof_bridge.lean. The reviewed file matches HEAD and was not modified.

submission.summary: Changed the main theorem’s root bound to `‖z‖ < r`, matching the original open root disk and excluding the zero-radius counterexample. Updated its docstring and counterexample explanation to use `1 < s < r`; all variants and attributes remain unchanged. The required compile passes with only expected `sorry` warnings, and independent Lean checks confirm the cited proof construction supports the corrected statement.
